Class ColumnReader

Namespace
ParquetNeo

ParquetNeo.dll

Reads the values of one column chunk, a batch at a time. Obtain it from OpenColumn(int) and dispose it when done, which returns its buffers to the pool.

public sealed class ColumnReader : IDisposable

Remarks

A required column fills values and reads values.Length rows. An optional column also takes a definitionLevels span, whose length is the number of entries requested: it receives 0 for a null and 1 for a value, and values receives only the non-null values, packed at the start. Because any row may hold a value, values needs room for as many entries as there are rows requested. The result says how many rows and values were read; 0 rows means the chunk is exhausted.

Pages are read one at a time, so memory stays bounded by the largest page. Not thread safe.

ReadBatch(Span<DateTime>, Span<int>, Span<int>)

Reads a TIMESTAMP column in any unit as DateTime: UTC when the column is adjusted to UTC, otherwise Unspecified. A moment outside the years 1 to 9999 is a ValueConversionException. An INT96 column, the deprecated timestamp of Impala, Hive and older Spark, is read too: it has no time zone, so its values are Unspecified. INT96 columns can be read but not written.

public BatchRead ReadBatch(Span<DateTime> values, Span<int> definitionLevels = default, Span<int> repetitionLevels = default)

BatchRead

ReadBatch(Span<decimal>, Span<int>, Span<int>)

Reads a DECIMAL column of any physical type (INT32, INT64, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY or BYTE_ARRAY) as decimal. A decimal holds 96 bits and a scale of up to 28, so a column with a larger scale is an ArgumentException and a larger stored value is a ValueConversionException. A column of BYTE_ARRAY values may return fewer values than requested, as ReadByteArrays(Span<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>, Span<int>, Span<int>) does.

ReadStrings(Span<string>, Span<int>, Span<int>)

Reads a BYTE_ARRAY column that is annotated STRING, ENUM or JSON, or not annotated, as UTF-8 text. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are a ValueConversionException. Like ReadByteArrays(Span<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>, Span<int>, Span<int>), a batch ends at the end of a page and may return fewer values than requested.
